messages:
Maria: Quick sync re: post-RFC operational playbook for kernel flag rollouts. Need to lock down concrete gating criteria and an emergency escape path.

Alex: Sounds good. Can we list the gating signals first?

Maria: Proposed gating signals:
- smoke_eval_pass (small prompt set match)
- p95_latency_ms within threshold
- exception_rate_pct below threshold
- model_quality_regression_pct under X
- min_qps to avoid noisy stats

Sandeep: Add a determinism check for quantized kernels. We had nondeterministic tokenization-related diffs once.

Lin: Rollout plan suggestion: split by traffic tag (routing key) to avoid tenant-wide flips. Steps: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Pause at each step for N minutes and run checks.

Jen: For checks, we should differentiate between perf-only and semantic-only failures. Perf fails can auto-roll back; semantic regression needs human review.

Maria: Agreed. Perf rollbacks automatic; semantic rollback creates a P1 ticket and pauses the rollout.

Alex: How do we capture which kernel binary was used for each request to trace issues?

Jen: Emit these telemetry fields: kernel_variant, kernel_sha, quant_profile, route_reason. Also attach a tiny span: route_reason and chosen_kernel.

Sandeep: Fallback ordering must be explicit in the model flag. Prefer to order by correctness -> latency -> cost. So cpu-quant last.

Maria: Example flag JSON for the flag service (compact):
```
{
  "model_id": "customer-x/large-1",
  "flags": {
    "primary_kernel": "kv-opt-2024-07",
    "fallback_kernels": ["kv-stable-2023","cpu-quant-8bit"],
    "min_qps": 10,
    "rollout_steps_pct": [0.5,2,10,50,100],
    "hold_minutes": 20,
    "checks": {
      "p95_latency_ms": 180,
      "exception_rate_pct": 0.25,
      "eval_regression_pct": 0.8
    }
  }
}
```

Lin: On ownership: model-platform owns onboarding and default flags; runtime infra owns the rollout orchestration and telemetry. Ops owns emergency escapes.

Alex: API idea: POST /admin/flags/{model}/override {kernel, ttl, reason}. Overrides must write to audit log and emit an incident tag. No permanent overrides without a RFC.

Maria: We'll add an enforcement rule: overrides expire automatically; team must tie long-lived changes to a ticket and RFC.

Sandeep: Canary automation: before increasing percent, run a determinism+semantic smoke job against canary instances (20 prompts) and require zero unexpected token diffs above threshold.

Jen: Also: add a lightweight cost estimate in the flag metadata (expected tokens/sec improvement, est_cost_delta) so product/finance can opt-in for aggressive perf kernels.

deploy-bot: Canary triggered: model=customer-x/large-1 kernel=kv-opt-2024-07 step=0.5% region=us-east-1 link=https://ci.internal/canaries/879

Alex: Canary baseline: p50=55ms p95=140ms error_rate=0.0% smoke_eval_match=100% so far.

Lin: Note: If model is low-volume (<min_qps) we should hold off and run offline eval instead of a live canary.

Maria: Action items: 
- @Alex: draft override API + audit schema (PR)
- @Sandeep: add smoke determinism checks to canary pipeline (ticket)
- @Jen: add telemetry fields + tracing span (PR)
- @Maria: update the post-RFC tracking board with these playbook rules and make templates for flag JSON

Alex: I'll start the API draft today.

Sandeep: Filing ticket now.

Jen: I'll queue telemetry change.

Maria: Thanks. Closing note: keep rollouts per-model and explicit, gate on both perf and semantic signals, and make emergency escapes auditable and short-lived.
